caption:
Here is my list for my top pharmacy residency “non-negotiables”. 
These are the very few things that I thought about before making the commitment. (Of course I wish I could cover all the considerations!) 

If you are comfortable and accept all of these, residency could be your path after graduation👀

❌ Immediate Financial Independence: 
- If you absolutely need a high starting salary immediately to pay down debt or handle any expenses, delaying residency might be necessary. 
- In Canada, residents typically make between $30-60K depending on the province and program. 
- A new practicing pharmacist can start making $100K. 

❌ Strict 9-to-5 Work Schedule: 
- A lot of residents report working overtime, around 50-70 hours a week when you factor in patient work-ups and rotation projects. 
- It can follow you home depending on which program you are in. 
- Do your research on the company and residency. 

❌ Disinterest in Research/Projects: 
- Residency involves a major research project, presentations, and for you to showcase your work. 
- If you dread these kind of academic requirements and formal presentations, you may find residency difficult. 
- You are essentially both a student and pharmacist at the same time.

This stems from my current perspective on pharmacy residency since I am wrapping up mine & I work in retail pharmacy too. There are HUGE differences between these two jobs. 

(p.s. I am located in Canada 🇨🇦 so my experiences are tailored!)

Whether you’re a pharmacy student, making the leap into industry, or already navigating the corporate world, making the most of a multi-day event can feel overwhelming!!

Here is how to maximize your time, build real connections, and walk away with actual value:

1. Set targeted learning intentions
You probably won’t be able to attend every session you want. Pick a few key themes and stick to them. If the industry is buzzing about things like AI, automation, or regulatory intelligence, prioritize those and skip the ones that don’t directly serve your current growth goals.

2. You being in a non-traditional & unique career, is what you should lead with. 
Instead of just reciting your job title, tell your story and what you’re actually passionate about solving in the industry. It makes you infinitely more memorable! 

3. Follow the 48-hour rule
Collecting business cards means nothing if you don’t use them. Connect on LinkedIn within 48 hours while the conversation is still fresh.

👇 Save these tips to use as your game plan for your next industry event!

DAY 21/90 #90DaystoThrive Challenge

Let’s talk about where the majority of PharmD / Bachelor of Pharmacy work…

Retail/Community Pharmacy!! 

As a pharmacy student, we get experience working across different corporate chains, and sometimes independent pharmacies too. Most newly graduated pharmacists work in community because there is usually a bigger demand in this career path and more job availabilities. 

There are many reasons for this, but one big one is we’re seeing more current community pharmacists changing careers. This leaves openings for new grads to join. I know many people who love working in retail and many who actually say they hate it. 

It’s definitely not for everyone, and you have time to figure that out. Your career does not end when you’re done school and career advancement is always on your reach if you involve yourself in the pharmacy community. 

Those who like to work in retail pharmacy can move on to become leaders in manager, associate, or corporate head office positions. If you enjoy the business/admin side of pharmacy, that could be up your alley!
